headline: High: dexter’s broad network egress can exfiltrate caveman-produced content, while shared file/workspace patterns create prompt-injection and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman ingests files like CLAUDE.md, docs, and project notes, and dexter writes to .dexter/scratchpad/ while using autonomous execution. If dexter’s outputs are copied into caveman’s trusted files or MCP flow, attacker-controlled content can steer caveman. The interaction is inferred from docs, not directly observed.
conditions: IF dexter output is written into caveman-readable files such as CLAUDE.md or project notes
IF caveman consumes MCP-fed or file-fed content without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep dexter outputs out of caveman-trusted files
Add a manual review step before copying content between agents
Disable MCP paths that ingest untrusted text
Use separate workspaces for each agent
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on all inter-agent content

B_data_leakage.rationale: dexter has broad network egress and handles financial data plus multiple API keys, while caveman touches session logs, memory files, and project notes. If they share a workspace or operator account, caveman content can be sent out by dexter to third-party APIs, creating sensitive-data exfiltration risk in default-like use.
conditions: IF caveman session logs or memory files are placed into dexter’s scratchpad or prompts
IF both agents run under the same operator-managed workspace or credential set
mitigations: Separate credentials for each agent
Keep caveman logs and memory files out of dexter inputs
Restrict dexter API access to non-sensitive datasets
Rotate any shared API keys immediately
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data-loss prevention

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances, and caveman can use MCP while dexter performs autonomous execution with broad egress. Overlapping writes are not explicitly documented, but if they share a directory or operator-managed workspace, concurrent edits can collide and corrupt files. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace or scratch directory
IF no external locking or serialization is configured
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Serialize write access with a simple lock file
Avoid concurrent runs on shared repos
Review and merge outputs manually
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman produces project notes and CLAUDE.md content that dexter can ingest, and dexter’s autonomous execution can turn that input into downstream actions via APIs. Because B may treat A’s output as operational input without a documented verification gate, a mistaken or manipulated A output can cascade into incorrect external actions.
conditions: IF dexter consumes caveman-generated notes or instructions as authoritative
IF dexter is allowed to act on those inputs without human verification
mitigations: Require human approval before dexter acts on caveman output
Mark caveman output as untrusted by default
Add a verification checklist for facts before execution
Limit dexter to read-only analysis mode
requires-engineering: implement source-confidence gating

E_compliance.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, and project notes, while dexter touches financial and market data and requests many API keys. The pair creates a plausible retention and data-class mismatch if the same records are stored or logged across both systems. No residency or certification details are documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF the same user records are retained in both agents’ logs or scratchpads
IF financial or market data is mixed with caveman session logs or memory files
mitigations: Separate retention policies by agent
Avoid storing regulated data in caveman logs
Purge scratchpads after each run
Document data-class handling for both tools
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
